pseudos.text: From the regulatory frontier in Brussels, the EU's competition pioneers have charted a course using the new Digital Markets Act as their compass. After a two-year investigative journey, they have navigated past a company's proposed detours and are now approaching a decisive checkpoint before the August recess. The American search engine navigator, who was exploring commercial territories within its own search results, now faces the prospect of a landmark penalty, a new enforcement instrument being forged to mark the boundaries of the digital realm. This would add to a legacy of fines, forging a new front on old ground.

A long expedition through procedural terrain is nearing its end. From its outpost in Brussels, the EU's rule enforcers initiated a journey under new digital statutes, seeking to map fair competition. The American tech giant, a pioneer in search, had its proposed route corrections rejected after more than two years of traversing the regulatory landscape. Now, as the summer recess looms, the explorers are preparing a final sanction—a potential nine-figure sum to demarcate a fresh exclusion zone, building upon a decade of established enforcement trails.
